question.text: A 'Pure Offshore' AIF structure is one where:

answer.text: The AIF is pooled inside India but the manager is outside India
There is no intent to pool capital at the Indian domestic level; the pooling vehicle is fully offshore and invests into India via FVCI/FPI/FDI
All investors are Indian residents pooled via LRS
The AIF is registered under SEBI (AIF) Regulations but domiciled outside India

explanation.text: The Logic: Pure Offshore = the pooling vehicle is offshore (Mauritius, Singapore, etc.), no onshore AIF. The offshore fund invests into Indian investee companies via FVCI, FPI, or FDI routes. Used when India is just one of many geographies in a global portfolio. SEBI (AIF) Regulations do NOT apply to the pooling vehicle itself. The Trap: Option A describes an onshore-AIF-with-offshore-manager situation. Option C is fabricated. Option D is internally contradictory — SEBI (AIF) requires domestic domicile. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C/D cover this taxonomy. Pure offshore is diminishing with GAAR pressure. Manager's Pro-Tip: Pure offshore is losing ground to unified/master-feeder + GIFT-IFSC structures. For a new Cat III raise targeting foreign capital, evaluate GIFT-IFSC feeder over a pure-offshore Mauritius SPV for long-term substance.
